nodes.recap: chapter header - waking in the dark, the mutilation of losing her, the fire, dragging clear
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 24          |
-------------------------------


$CYour head is splitting.##

Hundreds of lights dance behind your eyes and a strong pins-and-needles
pervades everything.# You are shaking, in the dark.#
Before you are even fully conscious, before the pain makes sense,
your first thought is of Saberinne.##

You feel mutilated.# Your mind has closed back in on itself,
alone, without the sustaining presence of hers,
without any awareness beyond your own body.#
It is worse than going suddenly blind and deaf at once.##

You groan at the mental pain, which is louder than the physical.#
You spend long minutes writhing on the ground,
losing consciousness more than once.##

Then the smell of smoke cuts through everything and brings you back:
a tree a few meters away is on fire.# You roll over, and see it,
and drag yourself clear, coughing.# You crawl through the mud
under the relentless rain, struggling to breathe,
until the darkness takes you again, one more time.##

$W----$C##

The ceiling is white.# A different white from Saberinne's hall,
hospital white, fluorescent, uniform, smelling of disinfectant,
with a monitor beeping at measured, reassuring intervals.##

You must have been brought here.# And then you hear her voice.

nodes.recap: hospital - the lie to spare her [DECISION: reply, tell the truth or spare her, converges] - the storm interrupted - the smile that means his humour is back

dialogues.precomment: Your mother is looking at you from beside the bed, her face open with fear.
dialogues.line: Oh my God, Kriss, how are you?

dialogues.precomment:
The truth is right there, entire: that you feel terrible, far worse than you look,
that some small, honest part of you would rather not have woken up at all.#
But you look at her face, and the words will not come.

dialogues.comment: She throws herself onto your neck, crying from fright.

dialogues.line: Come on, mom.# It's over.# I'm fine now...

dialogues.precomment: When she finally recovers enough to pull back and look at you, she asks:
dialogues.line: You were struck by lightning!# Do you realize?

dialogues.precomment:
You look at her without expression.# After everything you have been through,
it does not seem like a very improbable event.
you start to say, but she is already interrupting you.
dialogues.comment:
You try to smile.# She smiles back, satisfied - if your sense of humour
is already returning, it must be a good sign.##

Really, more than anything, you want to cry.

nodes.recap: discharge - drive home in silence - Sunday surrounded by family
nodes.text:
They discharge you the next day.# Coming home, you say nothing.
You watch your world move past the window in the rain,
and you think of Noi-Hert.# You cannot believe it was imagination.
You walked on that earth, breathed that air, ate food
that gave you strength, and really, truly spoke with your friends there.##

And Saberinne...##

A knot in your throat stops every other thought.
You turn to the window to hide your eyes.##

The next day is Sunday: you would not have gone to school anyway.#
Your family surrounds you for the whole day, worried and warm,
and for long stretches of it you almost manage not to think
about your friends, lost somewhere in the future of a second Earth.

nodes.recap: Sunday dinner - the argument about going back to school - the resolve, not knowing how true his father's words are

dialogues.precomment:
Over dinner, your mother finally asks the question she has
clearly been holding in all day.
dialogues.line: Are you sure you want to go back to school?
Yes.# I couldn't stand another day inside this house...

dialogues.precomment: Your father sets down his fork.
dialogues.line:
But you haven't fully recovered.# You had a bad shock -
you should rest, stay in bed.
dialogues.comment: He has no idea how true that is.

dialogues.line: No, dad.# I've decided.# I need to get back to my normal life...
dialogues.comment:
Your parents look at you without understanding.# You see the worry
and confusion in their faces, so you stand, and say,
before heading to your room:

dialogues.line: Believe me.# It's better this way.
dialogues.comment:
You have to readjust yourself, mentally too, to your own world, your own life.#
You cannot go on living in Saberinne with your mind.# You would not survive it.#
You would go mad.##

After more than an hour, you manage to fall asleep.# And you dream of her.

nodes.recap: the dream of her - waking with tears - the window
nodes.text:
She is close, in the dream, and beautiful, and she is speaking to you,
and you can hear again that marvelous voice that moves every atom
in your body.# You can see her smile.# You can breathe her scent.##

You wake with tears on your face.# You check the time: it is deep night.##

You go to the window, wrap yourself in a blanket, and look at the
sleeping city.# The sky has cleared.# Despite the glow of the streetlights
you can make out a scatter of stars, and here and there, a constellation.##

You think of throwing your thought out toward those depths,
the way you could only do on Noi-Hert.

nodes.recap: the window [DECISION: reach for her or resist - it fails either way]
nodes.text:
You stand at the window a long moment,
the city asleep below you, the blanket heavy on your shoulders.##

$D[Select with arrow keys and press enter]$C.

choices.desc: Reach for her, one more time.

nodes.recap: reach branch - the call goes out, nothing answers, mind gone mute
nodes.text:
You throw your thought outward, with an immense, lonely melancholy,
toward those depths, knowing that somewhere out there
that same planet is turning, silently, around its star,
with no trace of intelligent life on it that could ever answer.##

Nothing answers.# Your mind has gone mute again.##

Frustrated, with the sadness crushing your chest,
you go back to sleep.

nodes.recap: resist branch - tries not to, does it anyway, nothing answers, mind gone mute
nodes.text:
You tell yourself it is pointless, that reaching for her again will only
make tomorrow harder, that you decided this two nights ago on the drive home.##

But your thought is already moving before you have finished deciding,
out through the glass and into the dark, the way it moved without asking
your permission on every one of those desert nights, toward those depths,
knowing that somewhere out there that same planet is turning, silently,
around its star, with no trace of intelligent life on it that could ever answer.##

Nothing answers.# Your mind has gone mute again.##

Frustrated, with the sadness crushing your chest,
you go back to sleep.

nodes.recap: the alarm - morning routine - the scarred tree - classmates greet him warmly
nodes.text:
The alarm rings earlier than you would like.# You have to get up now,
or you will be late.# With an effort of will you force yourself
to the bathroom, then breakfast, then out the door.##

The morning air sharpens your senses.# You pull your jacket tighter
and tell yourself that sooner or later you will forget all of this,
whatever you think or feel right now.##

You pass the tree, the one where everything began, and where
everything ended.# The rain put the fire out.# Many of its leaves
are charred, and some branches are bare and blackened.#
That tree, too, will carry the scar of this.##

You arrive early, in fact, ahead of everyone, and take your usual seat.#
One by one your classmates come in and greet you warmly,
making sure you're alright, wanting the details of the accident.

nodes.recap: teacher enters - the whisper about the new girl - Sabrina introduced

dialogues.precomment:
At last the teacher comes in, and everyone sits.# Meanwhile a girl has
slipped in as well, and gone to introduce herself, off to the side.#
The classmate in the row behind you leans forward and whispers:
dialogues.line: Hey, Kriss.# There's a new student today.
dialogues.comment: He nods toward the door.# You keep your eyes on your notebook.

dialogues.precomment: Then, from the front of the room:
dialogues.line: Please, sit down, Sabrina.# Everybody give her a warm welcome!

nodes.text:
You look up.##

Her eyes are green.##

Exactly that particular green, the specific green
of deep water when the sun is at exactly the right angle,
the only green that exists in exactly one way on two worlds.##

Time stops.# The same way it stopped in the elliptical hall.##

You recognize that gaze, and the curve of that smile, instantly,
and for one wild heartbeat you are almost certain
you can feel her mind brush against yours again.##

An instant that lasts a million years.

nodes.recap: say the name or not [DECISION: it comes out either way]
nodes.text:
The classroom around you does not exist,
for this one suspended second of silence.##

$D[Select with arrow keys and press enter]$C.

nodes.recap: hold-back branch - tries to swallow it, fails
nodes.text:
You try.# You clamp down on it, tell yourself this is a rain-soaked
classroom of sixteen-year-olds, that the word climbing your throat
belongs to another world entirely.##

It comes out anyway.

You do not even try to stop it.##

It is already leaving your mouth before you have decided to speak.

nodes.recap: Saberinne! - her correction - the empty seat - the closing line

dialogues.precomment:
She looks at you, startled.# You are gripping the edge of your desk,
breathing like you have run a mile.# She was not expecting a welcome
quite like this one.
dialogues.line: You must have misheard...# my name is Sabrina...
dialogues.comment:
She says it smiling despite herself.# You cannot stop staring,
and she holds your gaze, amused, steady, with those eyes.
- not giving much weight to the strange wordplay.

dialogues.precomment:
She walks between the desks, checking the few free seats, and stops
beside the one that has sat empty next to you for as long as you can remember.
dialogues.line: Do you mind if I sit here?

dialogues.precomment:
You stare at her, mouth open, unable to produce a single syllable,
unable to accept she is actually, physically in front of you.#
Some part of you is still certain this is a dream.
dialogues.comment:
You finally manage to stammer it out, amid the envious,
mocking laughter of your classmates.

dialogues.precomment:
She sits, and arranges her things.# After a moment she turns,
and looks at you in that way that makes your heart tear itself in half,
and says:
dialogues.line: You know, Kriss...# I have the impression I've seen you somewhere before.
